relevance.rationale: The monodromy of hypergeometric functions and the construction of non-lattice integral monodromy groups -- the source of the complex-hyperbolic lattice classification arising from cyclic covers of the projective line branched at marked points. The nearest thing to a consumer in the corpus is conj:gauge-hecke-realization, whose stated open residue is that faithfulness of a braid representation at generic parameters does not imply faithfulness of the specialisation at the substrate anchor. This theory does treat specialised braid/hypergeometric monodromy -- but at parameters on the unit circle (roots of unity, rational exponent data), whereas the corpus's anchor is a real number greater than one, off that locus entirely. So it does not settle the residue, and the corpus has no block on hypergeometric monodromy or on the moduli of five points on the line that would consume it (grep: no configuration-space or M_{0,5} thread; the braid group is introduced categorically and explicitly 'precedes any geometric realisation'). Scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing usable at the corpus's current blocks -- not a claim that hypergeometric-monodromy methods are excluded from the faithfulness question.

proposedActions.rationale: The one candidate target, conj:gauge-hecke-realization, needs faithfulness at a real anchor greater than one; the classification here lives at root-of-unity parameters. Citing it would suggest a bearing on the residue that it does not have.
